claims.statement: Canonical actor-scoped response usage revisions, topology-neutral root/child actor declarations, durable response-replacement and affiliation reducers, Claude workflow and native team correlation, independent frozen sanitized-oracle parity, and a versioned public v2 query across Rust, N-API, and the transport-neutral SDK are implemented. Writer-owned pack readiness moves provider-stream commits through Pending to a query-visible Ready or Unavailable barrier without cursor fabrication or unrelated-stream churn, and applicable quarantine gaps fail closed until replay. Schema v48 persists normalized support-bound source/family coverage, exposed through a generic bounded getFactFamilyCoverage contract across Rust, N-API, and the transport-neutral SDK. Its fixed-snapshot pages contain only opaque common references and deterministically cover points, absences, and errors. Readiness and replacement coverage share one administrative transaction: deterministic failures at every precommit seam roll back both, while after-commit acknowledgement loss survives reopen and retries as an equal no-op. The common coordinator uses coverage as a frozen per-object generation baseline for explicit usage-v2 replay: it marks Pending before reads, retracts old-generation contributions with the first replacement slice, resumes bounded work after restart, and publishes complete replacement coverage only after every provider drains. Public replay is exposed by low-level N-API and the sole-owner observation host as a stale-safe compare-and-set over scope, source, digest, and coverage commit; the host injects configured roots while the transport-neutral query/IPC client remains read-only. Schema v49 adds source-instance-scoped query-selection contract v1: an absent row is immutable legacy.usage@1 epoch zero, promotion atomically compare-and-sets the prior tuple and revalidates one Ready/complete v2 barrier, failed guards create no commit, explicit rollback remains available while v2 is unhealthy, and crash-seam plus acknowledgement-loss tests prove atomic idempotence. N-API and the sole-owner host expose promotion/rollback while the transport-neutral client remains read-only, and the v2 page returns selection, readiness, rows, and aggregates under one snapshot. A bounded composite totals query negotiates every contributing source and returns no unlabeled mixed or unready total. A separate read-only compatibility query compares retained legacy and eligible v2 arms under one snapshot, reports directional or incomparable bucket deltas, derives a request-order-independent opaque comparison reference, and feeds only fixed owner-lifetime sample counters; it does not persist paths, scopes, response evidence, or per-sample rows. Coverage membership is streamed with bounded memory, and permanent diagnostics carry conservative unscoped or non-empty capability-scoped consequences so unrelated retained projection loss remains auditable without contaminating usage-v2 readiness. Common tests prove atomic administrative and selection crash recovery, snapshot-bound pagination, stale-cursor rejection, reference privacy, replay/selection authorization, non-mixing two-source aggregation, expected repeated-response divergence, explicit unknown-bucket incomparability, bounded telemetry, unhealthy-v2 rollback with retained shadow rows, actor and present-affiliation filtering, late workflow/team regrouping plus removal, ambiguity, generation retraction, repaired-gap recovery, and restart continuation without duplicate responses. An aggregate-only private-corpus experiment on a stable ephemeral clone matched an independent census exactly across 149,369 responses, 5,044 actors, 854 sessions, the root/child partition, model/fallback coverage, and all four token totals; all 5,182 transcript objects reached complete Ready v1 coverage with zero unknown buckets. Decoder contract 20 derives the root team edge only from team-config lead-session evidence plus an exactly-one lead match, preserves zero or multiple matches as unknown, and derives child membership only from path-owned subagent metadata team/name evidence. Sanitized fixtures and an end-to-end durable query test prove shared canonical team/member keys, filtering without copied usage, and snapshot edit/deletion retraction. An aggregate-only native-shape census found 26 valid configs with 26 unique lead-member matches and 20 current child joins with zero ambiguity. A representative external compatibility-window report, effective model/effort/mode, and interaction lifecycle remain required before support promotion.
